title: Say what each leaf is for

teaching.summary: The questions on this tree are already written. What is missing is what its answers mean: drop one apple into each empty leaf to say what that leaf is for, then test it against nine real apples out of the training set.
teaching.theory: A tree asks one question at a time. An apple goes in at the top, follows the first branch whose question it answers yes to, and comes to rest in exactly one leaf — and that leaf is the tree's answer for it. Nothing else about the apple matters: two apples that answer every question the same way get the same verdict, however different they look to you. That is what makes a tree readable, and it is also where one can be honestly wrong. If the numbers a tree asks about do not separate what you care about, no labelling of its leaves can rescue it.

disclosure: The two questions this tree asks were given to you. Choosing the questions — which measurement to cut, and where to cut it — is the whole of what fitting a tree is, and the model this lesson introduces chooses its own.
